coverage_gaps.description: Almost nothing surfaced from consultancies or academia specifically on ATM and POS terminal estate economics (acceptance-network sizing, ATM interchange, merchant acquiring cost studies) — the searches skewed to consumer payment behaviour.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Targeted HU queries on 'POS terminál elfogadóhelyek száma tanulmány', 'ATM hálózat költség elemzés', 'kereskedői elfogadás kutatás', and check Corvinus/BGE theses which often size acceptance networks.

coverage_gaps.description: No page in this cell was fetched and confirmed; all candidates rest on search-result evidence. Gating (registration walls on KPMG/Deloitte report downloads) is inferred, not observed.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Let the deterministic liveness/access pass fetch each source_url and example_url and record real HTTP status plus any registration wall; do not treat any single failure as death.

coverage_gaps.description: English-language Hungary-focused academic output (e.g. Corvinus and CEU working papers in EN, international journals with HU payment datasets) was only lightly probed; EN coverage of this cell is thinner than HU.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run EN queries on Google Scholar / RePEc: 'Hungary payment habits survey', 'cash usage Hungary card acceptance', 'Corvinus working paper payments', and add CEU/RePEc-Szemle listings.

coverage_gaps.description: No aggregator/archive was identified that systematically indexes Hungarian consultancy reports (as opposed to news mentions) — discovery currently depends on trade media noticing a release.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Test whether an index exists (e.g. university library databases, MATASZ/PSZÁF-era archives, or Wayback captures of consultancy insight pages) and otherwise accept trade media as the primary discovery layer with scheduled crawling of each firm's insights page.

brief: Hungary's consultancy/academic layer on payments splits into three clusters: Big-4 and strategy firms (Deloitte HU with its Digital Banking Maturity local cuts, PwC HU's own 'Digitális Pénzügyi Körkép' consumer survey, KPMG HU financial services, McKinsey Budapest) publishing lead-generation thought leadership; commercial research houses (GKID/GKI Digital, NRC, eNET, plus the Mastercard-sponsored GKID 'Digitális Kereskedelmi Körkép') which own the only regular non-regulator series on online payment-method mix and cash-on-delivery share; and an academic tier centred on Corvinus, whose full texts sit in the open unipub and REAL repositories and whose payment-habits and cash-network work is often published through MNB paper series, Közgazdasági Szemle or the Banking Association's Gazdaság és Pénzügy. Discovery is best driven by pointer media (FinTechZone, Portfolio.hu, HWSW's deep eNET/GKI archive), since consultancy studies are announced through the press before or instead of being indexed anywhere. Main weaknesses of this cell: full research-house reports are commercial, EY Hungary shows no payments-specific output, and nothing found addresses ATM/POS acceptance-network economics — that topic needs its own targeted Hungarian-language sweep.
